# GTA6Box

> An independent GTA 6 guide: mission walkthroughs, the Leonida map, characters, cars, weapons, cheats, editions and PC news. Confirmed facts only, updated daily.

GTA6Box is an independent, unofficial fan guide to Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6). Each page states whether its information is confirmed by Rockstar Games, lists its sources and shows the date it was last updated. Content may be quoted with a link to the page.

# GTA 6 Cheats: All 61 Cheats, Codes and How to Unlock Them

URL: https://gta6box.com/cheats/gta-6-cheats/
Updated: 2026-11-26
Status: partly

- GTA 6 has 61 cheats in five groups; button codes are confirmed for 21 of them so far.
- Cheats unlock only after the main story (reported as 91 missions), and each cheat has its own unlock task.
- The money cheat is Up, Right, Down, Left, Up, Left, Down, Right for $250,000. Cheats switch off saving and trophies.

GTA 6 has 61 cheats, but none of them work until you finish the story. They come in five groups: player, combat, vehicle spawns, world and screen filters. Each one also has its own unlock task, such as shooting-range medals, races or collectibles. Button codes are confirmed for 21 cheats so far; the rest are listed below with their unlock tasks, and we add each code as soon as two independent sources agree on it. Rockstar has not released an official list, so this page is marked partly confirmed.
How to enter cheats in GTA 6

Finish the main story. Launch guides report 91 story missions; the Cheats section appears under the Progress tab after the credits.
Complete the unlock task for the cheat you want.
Save your game. Cheats turn saving off.
In free roam, press Up on the D-pad to open the phone.
Hold L1 + R1 on PS5 or LB + RB on Xbox Series X|S. Guides differ on the wording: some say to hold L1 (LB) first and then press R1 (RB).
Enter the code on the D-pad.

All codes use only the D-pad, so they are the same on PS5 and Xbox.
Code patterns

Vehicle spawn codes start with Left, Up, Right, Down.
The three ammo cheats share the opening Down, Up, Right, Down, Left, Left, Up.
The screen filter codes start with Down, Down, Up, Right, Right, Up, Left, Left.

Checked on November 20: still 18 confirmed codes
We compared seven code lists again the day after launch. The 18 codes above match on every list that includes them, and none of the lists contradicts another.

Drunk. A code for the Drunk cheat now appears on two sites, but one of them says the input comes from a single outlet's guide and is not widely corroborated. That is one source, not two, so it stays off the table until an independent guide or Rockstar confirms it.
Raise Wanted Level. Its code is on four lists. Three other guides still mark it as not found, so treat it as the least certain of the 18.
Cycle Weather. The code is agreed. The unlock task is not: guides say either finishing the story or revealing the whole map.
Everything else. No code has been published for the other 42 cheats.

Second check, later on November 20
We ran the comparison again against three more lists: GTABase, Beebom (updated November 19) and Red Bull. All three show the same 18 codes, input for input, and all three still mark the other 43 cheats as "to be announced", including Drunk. Nothing was added to or removed from the tables above.
Two details from that check:

Cycle Weather. All three lists give "finish the story" as the unlock task, which is now the more widely reported version.
Story length. The lists disagree on how many missions stand between you and the Cheats menu: Red Bull says 91, Beebom says 118. The condition itself, finishing the main story, is the same everywhere.

Beebom alone says a cheat can be switched off by entering its code again. One source is not enough, so treat that as unconfirmed.
Checked on November 21: no new codes
Two days after launch the count has not moved. GTABase's list, read again today, still shows 61 cheats with 18 codes and marks the other 43 as "to be announced". Its 18 codes are the same as ours, input for input, and so are the unlock tasks.
Beebom's list, updated on November 20 and read again in a second check today, agrees: 61 cheats, the same 18 codes, 43 still to be announced.
Two details from GTABase are worth knowing, although we have not yet seen a second guide state them:

Entering the code of a cheat you have not unlocked does nothing.
Saving stays off until you quit, so progress made after a cheat is lost when you leave; loading the earlier save restores trophies.

Third check on November 21: Drunk still unconfirmed
A later comparison the same day looked at four lists again.

GTABase and KeenGamer still give no code for Drunk. GTABase shows 18 codes; KeenGamer shows 17 and marks Raise Wanted Level as undiscovered.
GTABoom now counts 19 codes because it includes an input for Drunk. Its other 18 match ours input for input.
Dexerto shows an input for Drunk as well, but we could not read its table cleanly enough to compare every direction, and we noted earlier that the Drunk input traces back to a single outlet.

That is not two independent sources we can check against each other, so Drunk stays out of the table. No code was added, removed or changed today. Two lists also repeat the rule that saving stays off until you quit: GTABase and KeenGamer both say to save first and quit without saving to get trophies back.

What cheats switch off

Saving is disabled while a cheat is active.
Trophies and achievements cannot be earned in that session.
Cheats are for story mode free roam only.

Tips for unlocking cheats faster

Many unlock tasks count progress you make during the story, so play shooting ranges, races and workouts as you go.
Do challenge groups in pairs: five challenges unlock one vehicle, all of them unlock a second.
Unlock tasks that need your partner (hours together, store robberies, activities) are easiest to finish in free roam after the credits.

How we check this page

The list of 61 cheats and their unlock tasks matches across several independent launch guides.
A code is listed only when at least two independent guides show the same inputs.
The status stays "partly confirmed" until each code is entered in the released game. If a patch changes a code, we update the table and the date at the top.

Looking for the money code on its own? See GTA 6 money cheat. For police levels, see GTA 6 wanted level.

Q: Does GTA 6 have cheat codes?
A: Yes, according to early guides published the day before launch: 61 cheats, entered with the D-pad through the in-game phone. Rockstar has not published an official list.

Q: What is the GTA 6 money cheat?
A: Up, Right, Down, Left, Up, Left, Down, Right gives $250,000. It is reported to unlock after you finish the main story.

Q: Can you use cheats from the start of GTA 6?
A: No. The Cheats menu is reported to appear only after the main story is finished, and many cheats need an extra task, such as shooting-range medals or workouts.

Q: How many cheats are in GTA 6?
A: 61: 10 player cheats, 11 combat cheats, 21 vehicle spawns, 3 world cheats and 16 screen filters.

Q: Do cheats disable trophies and achievements in GTA 6?
A: Yes. Reports say an active cheat disables saving and blocks trophies and achievements for that session, so save first.

# GTA 6 Close Surveillance Walkthrough: Drone and All 6 Cameras

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-close-surveillance-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-26
Status: confirmed

- Close Surveillance is a Jason-only Chapter 4 mission that opens after Power Play; you meet Karim on the top floor of a parking garage in Ocean Beach.
- The whole mission is flown with a drone: listen in on Nate and Cisco, follow their car, then hide six cameras in an apartment.
- It pays no cash, but flying the drone back to the van earns a Professional bonus.

This GTA 6 Close Surveillance walkthrough covers the drone mission where Jason and Karim spy on Nate and Cisco to find out who their inside man at the airport is. There is no shooting and no driving until the last minute. Everything depends on keeping the drone close enough to listen and far enough away not to be noticed.
Before you start

Detail
Info

Mission
Close Surveillance (Chapter 4, VCIA Takedown setup)

Playable character
Jason only

Starts at
Top floor of the marked parking garage, Ocean Beach, Vice Beach

You meet
Karim, at his van

Requirement
Power Play

Reward
No cash; Professional bonus for returning the drone

The two guides credit a different mission giver: PowerPyx names Karim, GTABase names Raul. Either way, Karim is the person waiting for you.
Objectives
PowerPyx lists thirteen on-screen steps; GTABase groups the same route into ten.

Fly the drone to The Calique.
Search the roof for the bodybuilders.
Follow Nate and Francisco.
Search the alley for the bodybuilders' car.
Follow Nate and Francisco.
Enter the apartment.
Place cameras around the apartment.
Listen to the interrogation.
Escape the apartment.
Fly to the van.
Get in the car.
Drop Lucia in the alley.

Step-by-step
1. Meet Karim and launch the drone
Go up to the top floor of the garage. Karim handles the microphone and Jason flies. Both guides describe the controls the same way: the drone handles much like a helicopter, holds its height by itself, and the triggers move it up and down.
2. Find Nate and Cisco at The Calique
Fly to the marked building, a rooftop bar. Head for the white boxes on the roof; the two men are sitting under the smaller white shelter on the north side.
3. Listen in
Move close enough to fill the bar at the bottom of the screen. That bar is your range for the microphone.
When they leave by the elevator, do not follow them down. Fly to the alley on the right of the elevator to find Cisco's car.
4. Follow the car

Do
Don't

Stay high above the car
Drop to street level

Keep the bar in the green
Let the car get out of range

They stop once so Nate can collect something from a nearby building, then drive on to an apartment block.
5. Get into the apartment
Karim points out a balcony: it is the third one up, and its door is open. Fly in. GTABase gives the address as apartment 405; the man who lives there, Omar, runs baggage handling at the airport.
6. Place the six cameras
Omar walks around while you work. Watch the awareness indicator and stay in a different room from him.

#
Room
Spot

1
Living room
Beside the TV

2
Living room
Shelf on the opposite wall

3
Kitchen
Corner of the counter (after Omar leaves the kitchen)

4
Kitchen
Top of the fridge

5
Hall
Shelf near the front door

6
Bedroom
Shelf to the right of the bed (after Omar opens the bedroom door)

Tip: if Omar walks toward the drone, GTABase's advice is to tuck it out of sight and wait for him to leave the room before you carry on.
7. Watch the interrogation
Nate and Cisco arrive and lean on Omar. Switch between your cameras to keep them in view while they talk.
8. Get the drone out
Karim broadcasts through the drone's speaker by mistake. Fly out of the apartment at once, before the men find it, and return to the van on the street, marked with a green square.
Tip: bring the drone all the way back. Both guides say retrieving it is what earns the Professional bonus; GTABase adds that the bonus counts toward your Criminal Profile.
9. Drop Lucia off
After a scene at the van about the hard drive, get in the car with Lucia and drive her to the alley near Ajax Gym. The mission ends there.
Where players fail
Neither guide lists a formal fail condition. These are the points they warn about:

Losing the car. Dropping low to follow it costs you sight lines; height keeps the bar green.
Being noticed in the apartment. Place cameras only in rooms Omar has left.
Leaving the drone behind. You lose the Professional bonus if it does not make it back to the van.

100%
GTABase marks the mission as required

Close Surveillance is one of four setup jobs that open after Power Play. The others are Delivery Method, Team Building and Fully Catered, and all of them lead to the VCIA Takedown. The full order is in our GTA 6 mission list, and the heist chain is explained in GTA 6 heists.

Q: Where do the cameras go in the GTA 6 Close Surveillance walkthrough?
A: Six spots: beside the TV and on the shelf opposite it in the living room, the corner of the kitchen counter, the top of the fridge, the shelf by the front door, and the shelf to the right of the bed.

Q: How do you start Close Surveillance in GTA 6?
A: Finish Power Play, then take Jason to the marked parking garage in Ocean Beach, Vice Beach, and go up to the top floor to meet Karim at his van.

Q: What is the reward for Close Surveillance?
A: No cash. PowerPyx lists the reward as none, and both guides say that returning the drone to the van gives a Professional bonus.

Q: Can you fail Close Surveillance by being seen?
A: Neither guide lists a formal fail condition, but both tell you to watch the awareness indicator in the apartment and keep the drone in a different room from Omar.

This GTA 6 Delivery Method walkthrough covers Andrea's job for Jason: ride into the airport dressed as a food courier and put Lucia's details into the security system. # GTA 6 DLC: Is Story DLC Coming, and What You Can Buy Today

URL: https://gta6box.com/blog/gta-6-dlc/
Updated: 2026-11-26
Status: partly

- No GTA 6 story DLC, expansion or season pass has been announced by Rockstar Games or Take-Two as of November 26, 2026.
- The only extra content today is the Ultimate Edition's 16 items, the Vintage Vice City Pack and GTA+ perks; none of it adds missions.
- Rockstar's last two big games, GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, never received story DLC; GTA 4 received two expansions in 2009.

GTA 6 DLC has not been announced: as of November 26, 2026, Rockstar Games and Take-Two have not confirmed a story expansion, a season pass or any new missions for Grand Theft Auto VI. The game has been out for a week, and the question is already one of the most searched about it. This page separates what is on the record from what is guesswork: what Take-Two's chief executive actually said, which add-ons exist today, what Rockstar did after its previous games, and what to do with a finished save in the meantime.
How we checked: statements are included only where at least two reports agree on what was said and when. History comes from Rockstar's own release record. Leaks and "insider" claims are left out.

Has Rockstar announced GTA 6 DLC?
No. Three separate round-ups of the question reach the same answer, and nothing on Rockstar's site or in Take-Two's launch press release mentions post-launch story content. The release, dated November 20, is about sales and review scores; it names no future content at all.
Why it matters: any page that gives a name, date or price for GTA 6 story DLC today is inventing it. The honest answer is short, and it is "not yet, and maybe never".
What Take-Two has actually said
The closest thing to a statement came on Take-Two's earnings call on November 9, ten days before launch. Chief executive Strauss Zelnick was asked what players would do after the campaign, and about multiplayer.

What he was asked
What he said, in brief
What he did not say

What players do after the story
That there is plenty to do, and that with this series you can always keep playing
Anything about new missions

A multiplayer mode
No details
A date, a name or features

The wider franchise
That there is a great deal still to be done with Grand Theft Auto
What, or when

Reports of the call agree on the substance: confidence in how much the game contains, and no specifics on anything that comes after. ComicBook.com adds that Zelnick indicated Rockstar would move on to its next project after GTA 6, again without detail.
Why it matters: these are careful remarks on an investor call. They do not rule out DLC, and they do not promise it.
What you can add to GTA 6 today
There is paid extra content for GTA 6, but it is cosmetic and practical, not story.

Add-on
What it is

Tip: if a store listing or video calls one of these "the GTA 6 DLC", that is loose wording. None of them extends the story, and you can finish everything in the game without them.
The Ultimate Edition does not include future DLC
Some special editions of other games bundle a season pass. GTA 6's does not. The Ultimate Edition's extras are all available now, inside the launch game. Both HappyGamer and GTA6Gang make the same point: the editions differ in launch extras, not in any claim on future content.
Why it matters: there is no reason to buy the more expensive edition as insurance against missing an expansion. If one is ever sold, nothing published so far ties it to an edition.
What Rockstar did after its last four big games
Rockstar's history is the best evidence there is, and it points in two directions.

Game
Year
Story DLC?
Where later content went

The older pattern is story expansions within a year or so. The newer pattern, which has now held for more than a decade, is an online mode that receives the new content while the single-player game stays as it shipped.
Why it matters: anyone predicting GTA 6 story DLC is betting that Rockstar returns to how it worked in 2009. Anyone predicting none is betting on how it has worked since 2013.
Why GTA 5 never received its expansion
GTA 5 came close. A single-player expansion was in development and was dropped. Dan Houser, the Rockstar co-founder who left the company in 2020, talked about it in an interview in 2025, as reported by GamesRadar+: he said the expansion was about half done when it was abandoned, and that he liked the GTA 4 model of extra stories arriving afterwards.
Those are the views of someone who no longer works at Rockstar, about a decision made years ago. They show that story DLC was tried and shelved once before. They are not a plan for GTA 6.
Tip: treat any "GTA 6 will get the DLC that GTA 5 lost" headline as opinion.
An online mode is the more likely form of new content
Rockstar describes the launch game as a single-player experience. A new online mode has not been named, dated or detailed, as our GTA 6 online guide explains. Zelnick avoided questions about it on the November 9 call.
If the pattern of the last two games holds, new vehicles, missions and activities would arrive there, not in the story. That is an inference from history, not an announcement, and until Rockstar says something it should be read as one.
Why it matters: if you are waiting for more GTA 6 to play, an online launch is the thing to watch for first. A PC version is the other unannounced release people ask about.
Updates so far have added nothing new
GTA 6 has been patched, but the patches have been technical. Two updates arrived before launch, and Rockstar has published no patch notes that add content. Our GTA 6 update page tracks every version and its size.
Tip: a download prompt on your console is not DLC. Check the version number against the update page before assuming something new has been added.
What is not confirmed

Any story DLC, expansion or season pass. None has been announced.
A date or name for an online mode. Rockstar has given neither.
A PC release. Not announced.
Whether single-player will receive new content through free updates. Nothing has been said either way.
Claims from leaks, datamining or unnamed insiders. We do not repeat them, and none has been confirmed by Rockstar.

What to do after the story while you wait
The launch game holds far more than its missions. If the credits have rolled and you want more, there is a long list before any DLC would be needed.

Replay the finale. Guides report that after the credits you are placed back before the last mission; see GTA 6 ending explained.
Use the cheats. The cheat list unlocks only after the story, and each code has its own unlock condition: GTA 6 cheats.
Work through the challenges. There are 80, and they unlock vehicles and cheats: GTA 6 challenges.
Hunt the collectibles. Start from the collectibles hub.
Finish the optional missions. Strangers and Freaks lists them.
Aim for 100%. Every requirement can be finished in free roam after the story: 100% completion checklist.

What this means for you
Do not buy anything, or hold off buying anything, on the expectation of GTA 6 DLC. Nothing exists to plan around. The game sold 32.5 million units before it launched, as our pre-order sales page explains, so Rockstar has every commercial reason to keep players engaged; how it chooses to do that is the open question. For now, the game on your console is the whole of GTA 6.
What we will add to this page

Any announcement from Rockstar or Take-Two about story content, with the date and source.
Details of an online mode when it is named or dated.
New paid add-ons if they appear on the PlayStation or Xbox stores.
Remarks from Take-Two's next earnings call that bear on post-launch plans.

Q: Will there be GTA 6 DLC?
A: Nothing has been announced. As of November 26, 2026, neither Rockstar Games nor Take-Two has confirmed story DLC, an expansion or a season pass for GTA 6.

Q: Did GTA 5 have story DLC?
A: No. A single-player expansion was started and abandoned; Dan Houser, the former Rockstar co-founder, said in 2025 that it was about half done when it was dropped. All of GTA 5's later content went to GTA Online.

Q: Does the GTA 6 Ultimate Edition include future DLC?
A: No. It includes the full game and 16 extra in-game items. Nothing in either edition promises a future story expansion.

This GTA 6 Fully Catered walkthrough covers Raul's request for an airport catering truck, the last piece of equipment the crew needs for the airport job. # GTA 6 Headliners Walkthrough: Best VIP Table Choices at VYB

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-headliners-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-26
Status: confirmed

- Headliners is the last mission for Dre'Quan in Chapter 4; either lead starts it at Club VYB in Washington Beach once the airport setup jobs are done.
- Your VIP table choices set the payout, which tops out at around $50,000, and the mission also unlocks the Brass Knuckles.
- Both guides call the upstairs fight the toughest melee fight in the game: dodge, then use the knife from the bar counter.

This GTA 6 Headliners walkthrough covers the Dimez' launch party at Club VYB, where Jason and Lucia run the door, the lights and the VIP tables before the night goes wrong. It is the one mission in this part of the story where your choices change the payout, so the table picks are worth getting right.
Before you start

Detail

Objectives
PowerPyx lists thirteen on-screen steps.

Step-by-step
1. Tour the club and test the lights
Find Dre'Quan near the entrance and follow him around. Then, as Lucia, go to the DJ booth and try the lights and effects. Use the exit prompt when you are done.
2. Assign the VIP tables (Jason)
Each guest shows two numbers: an offer, paid up front, and a followers count, which can bring in more money later. You have three tables.

Guest

3. Look after the guests (Lucia)

Maleek Rivers: go to his booth. He wants the lights to pick him out. Both guides recommend agreeing, because of his following.
KD: if you let him in, Dre'Quan sends you to his table. Agree to the photo and take a picture of him with his group.

4. Work the door (Jason)
In the lobby, a man claims he has already been inside. You can throw him out or let him stay; neither guide ties a consequence to it. Go out front to Dre'Quan and, when the cars pull up, open the door of the one on his right. Follow him back in, then lead the group down the stairs to the dance floor and into the VIP area.
5. Free up a table
Dre'Quan needs a table back, so one of your three groups has to move.
Tip: both guides say to move the Game Developer if you seated them. You keep their $50,000 offer, they bring few extra followers, and they accept the "upgrade" story most easily.

DWNPLY and his crew take over the stage. From the green room, follow Jason onto the balcony, drop to the lower level and go to the front right, directly below DWNPLY. Pull him off the stage. When his crew grabs Lucia, mash the prompt to break free and fight off the men who attack.

Jason takes one of his brass knuckles and finishes the fight

Back in the green room as Lucia, hit DWNPLY the moment the scene ends to take his gun and knock him out. Then join the dance floor: dance or watch the set. When Dre'Quan asks whether you want to stay or leave, either answer leads to the final scene.
Where players fail
Neither guide lists a formal fail condition. The hard parts are these:

The upstairs fight. PowerPyx calls him the strongest melee opponent in the game, and GTABase the toughest brawler. Trading punches does not work; dodging does.
The green room. Be ready to strike DWNPLY as soon as you regain control.
The table picks. A weak choice costs money, not the mission.

Q: What are the best VIP table choices in the GTA 6 Headliners walkthrough?
A: Both guides suggest Donatello Lambrini (most followers), the Game Developer (highest upfront offer) and KD (second-most followers). When asked to free a table, move the Game Developer: you keep the $50,000 offer.

# GTA 6 Heists: Both Story Heists, Setup Missions and Robberies

URL: https://gta6box.com/blog/gta-6-heists/
Updated: 2026-11-26
Status: partly

- GTA 6 has two story heists: the Cartel Heist at Sinfrontera National Bank in Chapter 3 and the VCIA Takedown at the airport in Chapter 4.
- Each is a chain of setup missions; walkthrough lists tag eight missions for the Cartel Heist and fifteen for the VCIA Takedown.
- Heists cannot be replayed. The Cartel Heist pays $120,000 according to two guides; the VCIA Takedown pays $250,000.

GTA 6 heists come in two sizes: two big story heists, the Cartel Heist and the VCIA Takedown, and a long list of smaller robberies you can run between missions. The story heists are multi-mission operations that close out Chapter 3 and dominate Chapter 4. This page lists every setup mission in order, the smaller jobs that lead up to them, the tools and safe codes confirmed so far, and what guides have not yet agreed on.
Mission names and order here match in two independent walkthrough lists, PowerPyx and GTABase. Where only one source reports something, we say so.

How heists work in GTA 6
A heist is not one mission. It is a chain: scouting the target, recruiting people, stealing equipment, a planning step and then the job itself. Lists mark the planning steps (Heist Planning, Heist Plans in Place) as their own entries, though PowerPyx has no walkthrough page for them, which suggests they are short.
Why it matters: setup missions are split between the two leads. Several are marked for Jason only or Lucia only, so if a heist seems stalled, switch character and check the map. The controls are in how to switch characters in GTA 6.
Who runs the heists: Raul Bautista
Rockstar introduced Raul Bautista before launch as an experienced bank robber who is always looking for talent. In the game he tests the pair before he trusts them. Lucia's first job for him is Car Service, a car theft from a gang chop shop, and the missions that follow lead to his crew.
Tip: Raul's missions arrive by message after a wait, not from a map marker you can visit at will. If nothing new appears, let a day of game time pass.

The free-roam robbery system
Outside missions, the map index has a Robberies section that lists targets. Guides describe these types:

Stores, restaurants and gas stations, held up at the register.
Smash 'n' Grabs: jewelry stores and pawn shops.
Banks and Payday Loan stores.
Bank vaults, which open late in Chapter 4. Guides report $100,000 or more per vault and an instant four-star wanted level.
Gang operations: guarded compounds with cash and valuables.
Safes and ATMs, including ATMs you can pull out with a winch.

The 100% checklist counts them: 39 gang operations, 22 bank jobs, 7 Payday Loan jobs and 8 vaults, all of which are required. See GTA 6 100% completion. A silver trophy asks for five bank vaults.

Getting the money home
Stealing is half the job. Loot other than cash goes into a bag and has to reach a fence. Three open in early Chapter 3: Yasmani for jewelry and marked bills, Tyrone for goods and Randy for vehicles. Cash in your pocket is lost if you are wasted or busted, so deposit it at an ATM. The full breakdown is in how to make money in GTA 6, and police behaviour is in GTA 6 wanted level.
Missable missions before each heist
Two optional missions are marked time-sensitive and missable by both lists:

Race Against Yago in Chapter 3.
This Is a Free Call From… in Chapter 4, for Lucia.

PowerPyx says such missions show an hourglass on the map and that missing them does not affect trophies or 100%.
How GTA 6 heists differ from GTA 5
GTA 5 built its story around a handful of heists where you chose an approach and hired a crew from a board. For GTA 6, no guide we have read documents a choice of approach or crew, and GTABase's heist guide does not mention one. What is clearly different is scale: fifteen tagged missions for one heist is far more preparation than any GTA 5 job needed. Other changes are in GTA 6 new features.
What is not confirmed

The payouts are now confirmed. Both PowerPyx and GTABase list $120,000 for the Cartel Heist and $250,000 for the VCIA Takedown; see The Cartel Heist walkthrough and the VCIA Takedown walkthrough.
Approaches and crew. Whether you choose either.
Fail states and choices inside the two finales. We have not yet matched two walkthroughs.
Raul's Fleeca decoy. Now confirmed by two guides: see the First Impressions walkthrough.
That's Where the Money Is… Now covered: it is Yasmani's optional bank vault job, worth about $80,000. See the That's Where the Money Is… walkthrough.

What to do before each heist

Make a manual save in a spare slot. See how to save and why missions cannot be replayed.
Finish optional missions, especially any with an hourglass.
Sell loot and bank your cash.
Stock ammunition and healing items for both characters.
Check both characters' maps for a setup mission you have not started.

What this means for you
If you came for heists, expect to wait: the first one ends Chapter 3, many hours in. The game fills that time with smaller jobs that pay well and teach the same skills, and the free-roam robberies go on after the story. Treat the two story heists as the peaks and Yasmani's stores, vaults and gang operations as the regular income. For where the heists sit in the full story, see how many chapters are in GTA 6 and the mission list.
What we will add to this page

Step-by-step walkthroughs for each setup mission as two guides confirm them.
Any approach or crew choices, once verified.
More safe codes from Chapter 3 and Chapter 4.

Q: How many heists are in GTA 6?
A: Two story heists: the Cartel Heist in Chapter 3 and the VCIA Takedown in Chapter 4. Around them are smaller scripted robberies and a free-roam robbery system with banks, vaults and gang operations.

Q: What is the first heist in GTA 6?
A: The Cartel Heist, a job on Sinfrontera National Bank organised by Raul Bautista. It is the last mission of Chapter 3.

Q: Can you replay heists in GTA 6?
A: No. Missions cannot be replayed, so make a manual save before the final mission of each heist if you want to play it again.

Q: How much do GTA 6 heists pay?
A: PowerPyx and GTABase both list $120,000 for the Cartel Heist; both list $250,000 for the VCIA Takedown. Confirmed smaller payouts include $20,000 for Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs and $10,000 for Afternoon Delight.

# GTA 6 Pre-Order Sales: 32.5 Million Before Launch, Explained

URL: https://gta6box.com/blog/gta-6-pre-order-sales/
Updated: 2026-11-26
Status: confirmed

- Take-Two says GTA 6 sold 32.5 million units pre-release, which it calls a record across all platforms, and made $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales.
- Sensor Tower's tracker, which counts digital PS5 and Xbox pre-orders, ended lower: about 24.6 million units and $2.36 billion.
- By Sensor Tower's estimates, about 75% of pre-orders were on PlayStation and most buyers chose the $99.99 Ultimate Edition.

GTA 6 pre-order sales reached 32.5 million units before the game launched, according to Take-Two Interactive, which called it a record across all platforms. The company gave that figure on November 20, 2026, one day after release, together with $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales. Before that, every pre-order number in circulation was an outside estimate. This page sets out the official figure, the estimates that led up to it, why the two do not match, and what pre-order buyers should have received.
How we checked: the official numbers come from Take-Two's press release. Every estimate is attributed to the firm that made it and appears in at least two reports, or is marked with the single outlet that carried it.

The official number: 32.5 million units pre-release
Take-Two's press release is dated November 20, 2026. It says Grand Theft Auto VI "sold 32.5 million units pre-release" and describes that as a new record across all platforms. It is the only pre-order figure that comes from the company itself.
The release does not break the number down. It names no split between PlayStation and Xbox, between the two editions, or between digital and boxed copies. The Next Web noted that Take-Two did not say how the figure was calculated.
Why it matters: "pre-release" is Take-Two's word, and it is not defined. The safest reading is the plain one: units sold before November 19. Anything more specific is someone's interpretation.
The $3.79 billion is not a pre-order figure
The same release puts day-one retail sales at $3.79 billion. A footnote says this is based on company estimates through the end of November 19, worldwide. Take-Two calls it a record for entertainment in any medium.
That number covers more than pre-orders. A quick check shows why: $3.79 billion divided by 32.5 million units is roughly $117 a unit, which is more than the $99.99 Ultimate Edition costs in the US. The revenue figure therefore has to include copies bought on launch day itself, on top of the 32.5 million sold beforehand. That division is ours, not Take-Two's, and regional prices vary, but the direction is clear.
Tip: when a headline says GTA 6 "made $3.79 billion in pre-orders", it has joined two separate statements. The units are pre-release; the dollars run to the end of launch day.
How the estimates grew before launch
Until November 20 the only public numbers were Sensor Tower's estimates of digital pre-orders on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. They rose slowly for months and then very fast.

Sensor Tower's analyst said the total more than doubled in the last ten days before release. The estimate passed $1 billion about a week before launch, according to VICE.
Why it matters: most people did not pre-order in June. They waited for reviews, trailers and the final week. That pattern is worth remembering the next time an early pre-order estimate is used to predict a launch.
Why the official figure is higher than the tracker
Take-Two says 32.5 million. Sensor Tower's final estimate was about 24.6 million. Neither party has explained the gap of roughly eight million, but the two numbers do not measure the same thing.

Take-Two
Sensor Tower

Type

What it counts
"Units sold pre-release", not defined further

Boxed copies
Not stated
Not included, according to VICE

Published
November 20, 2026
Updated through the pre-order period

VICE pointed out before launch that the tracker covered digital copies only, so pre-orders of the physical edition were unknown. That is the most likely source of the difference, but it has not been confirmed by either side.
PlayStation vs Xbox
By Sensor Tower's estimate, PlayStation accounted for about 75% of pre-order revenue and Xbox for about 25%. VICE reported the same three-quarters share in the November 16 update. Wccftech adds that PlayStation pre-orders opened a day before Xbox's and that the split barely moved afterwards.
Both platform holders made their own claims on November 10: Sony said GTA 6 was the most pre-ordered game in the history of the PlayStation Store, and Microsoft said the same of its store. Neither gave a count. For the hardware side of that split, see GTA 6 platforms.
Why it matters: there is no official platform breakdown. The 75% figure is an estimate of digital pre-orders, not a statement about the 32.5 million.
Most pre-orders were for the Ultimate Edition
Wccftech, reporting Sensor Tower's data, says 82% of pre-orders were for the $99.99 Ultimate Edition and 18% for the $79.99 Standard Edition. This is a single-outlet figure, so treat it with some caution. It does fit the revenue numbers: the tracker's totals work out to roughly $96 or $97 a unit at both the November 16 and final readings, close to the Ultimate price.
Tip: if you bought the Standard Edition and are wondering what the other four in five buyers got, the difference is 16 in-game items, none of them needed for the story. Our price and editions guide compares the two.

In the same tracker, GTA 6's pre-order revenue is more than three times the previous record. Against its own predecessor, GTA 6 sold almost three times as many units before launch as GTA 5 sold on its first day, which our sales page puts at 11.21 million.
Why it matters: the GTA 5 comparison flatters GTA 6 slightly, because the 2013 figures count sales after launch and the 2026 figure counts sales before it. It is still the larger number by a wide margin.
What Take-Two said before launch
Take-Two avoided numbers until the game was out. On its earnings call on November 9, chief executive Strauss Zelnick said pre-orders were far in excess of the company's expectations, while adding that the company was not ready to declare victory. The first hard figure came eleven days later, in the launch release, alongside a statement from Rockstar president Sam Houser thanking players.
For what the game cost to make, and how quickly these sales cover it, see how much GTA 6 cost to make.
What is not confirmed

How the 32.5 million was counted. Take-Two has not said whether it includes boxed copies shipped to shops, digital pre-orders only, or both.
An official platform or edition split. The 75% and 82% figures are Sensor Tower estimates.
Pre-order revenue on its own. The $3.79 billion includes launch day; the $2.36 billion is an estimate.
Sales since launch day. Take-Two has published nothing after November 19. Weekend and first-week totals quoted online are analyst estimates.
Pre-orders by country. None of the reports we checked gives a regional breakdown.

If you pre-ordered: check what you received
Pre-orders came with extras, and they are easy to overlook once you are playing.

Vintage Vice City Pack. Included with pre-orders and with any copy bought before November 20, 2026. Our Vintage Vice City Pack guide lists the contents.
One month of GTA+. Included with digital pre-orders of either edition. Check when the free month ends if you do not want it to renew.
Ultimate Edition items. If you bought the $99.99 edition, confirm the extra items are showing in game.
Pre-load. Pre-order buyers could download ahead of release; there was no early play. See GTA 6 early access for what each edition did and did not unlock.
Missing something? Restore licences on your console first, then contact the store you bought from, with your order confirmation to hand.

What this means for you
For players, the pre-order record changes nothing about the game on your console. It does say something about what comes next. A launch this large gives Rockstar every reason to keep supporting the game, and it makes the unanswered questions, a PC version and an online mode, a matter of when they are announced. The critical response was just as strong: see our GTA 6 reviews round-up.
What we will add to this page

Any clarification from Take-Two on what "pre-release" covers.
Official platform, edition or digital-versus-physical splits, if they are published.
Take-Two's next earnings report, which should carry the next official sales figures.
First-week and first-month totals once the company, not an analyst, reports them.

Q: How many GTA 6 pre-order sales were there?
A: Take-Two announced on November 20, 2026 that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million units pre-release. The company did not explain how the figure was calculated or split it by platform or edition.

Q: How much money did GTA 6 make from pre-orders?
A: There is no official pre-order revenue figure. Take-Two reported $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales worldwide, which runs to the end of November 19. Sensor Tower estimated about $2.36 billion from digital console pre-orders and launch day.

Q: Is GTA 6 the most pre-ordered game ever?
A: By every published measure, yes. Take-Two calls 32.5 million a record across all platforms, Sony and Microsoft each named it their store's most pre-ordered game, and Sensor Tower's estimate is more than three times its previous record.

- The choice in the penthouse changes nothing; the mission ends by starting Bird in the Hand, the first mission of Chapter 5.

This GTA 6 Starting From Zero walkthrough covers the final mission of Chapter 4, in which Jason and Lucia cross a city full of police to collect two things and meet a new contact. # GTA 6 Sunset Walkthrough: Chapter 4 Point of No Return

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-sunset-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-26
Status: confirmed

- Sunset starts when you collect the note at the Y Hotel front desk; both guides call it the Chapter 4 point of no return.
- Raul is in the small bathroom behind the second door on the left inside his houseboat at the marina.
- The escape is a dock shootout and a boat chase with limited ammo; shoot down the helicopter early.

This GTA 6 Sunset walkthrough covers the mission that ends free roam in Chapter 4: a visit to Raul's houseboat that turns into a running fight along the docks and out to sea. Read the checklist below before you pick up the note at the Y Hotel. Once you do, there is no going back to the open world for a long time.
Read this first: the point of no return
GTABase labels Sunset the Chapter 4 point of no return, and PowerPyx says the same: starting it carries the story into Chapter 5, and most of Chapter 5 has to be completed before the open world opens up again. The next mission, Starting From Zero, begins the moment this one ends.
Before you collect the note:

Finish the optional bank job That's Where the Money Is….
Clear any side missions and activities you care about.
Make a manual save in its own slot: how to save in GTA 6. Missions cannot be replayed.

This GTA 6 That's Where the Money Is walkthrough covers Yasmani's optional bank job, the first time the game lets you rob a vault on your own. The robbery itself is quick. The hard part is the drive away, because the police response starts at four stars and they open fire at once.

- Tie Up Loose Ends is a waiting mission that begins automatically after the VCIA Takedown; it has no map marker and no reward.
- Calling Valentina back, from either lead's phone or from the map, makes the next mission arrive sooner.
- It ends when you collect a note at the Y Hotel front desk, which starts Sunset, the point of no return for Chapter 4.

This GTA 6 Tie Up Loose Ends walkthrough explains the quiet stretch after the airport heist, where the only objective is to wait. There is nothing to fight and nowhere to go. What matters is knowing how to shorten the wait, and what to finish before you end it, because the mission that follows closes off free roam.

Q: How do you finish the GTA 6 Tie Up Loose Ends walkthrough faster?

Q: Why is Raul not calling in Tie Up Loose Ends?
A: He never does. GTABase says the call does not come however long you wait; Valentina's call is what moves the story on.

Q: What should you do during Tie Up Loose Ends?

Q: What do you need before the GTA 6 VCIA Takedown walkthrough begins?
A: Twelve setup missions: Making Gainz, Too Much Baggage, Amateur Hour, Cash Injections, Dirty Work, Adventures in Babysitting, Power Play, Close Surveillance, Delivery Method, Team Building, Fully Catered and Headliners.

# How Much Money Has GTA 6 Made? Copies Sold and Revenue So Far

URL: https://gta6box.com/blog/how-much-money-has-gta-6-made/
Updated: 2026-11-26
Status: partly

- Take-Two announced on November 20, 2026 that GTA 6 made $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales and sold 32.5 million units pre-release.
- Sensor Tower's earlier estimate, about 24.6 million copies and $2.36 billion through launch day, covered digital console sales, with roughly three in four on PlayStation.
- GTA 5's official first-day record was 11.21 million copies and $815.7 million in 2013.

How much money has GTA 6 made? Take-Two's official answer is $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales worldwide, with 32.5 million units sold before launch. The publisher announced both figures on November 20, 2026 and called it the biggest entertainment launch in history. Before that announcement the best number was an estimate from the analytics firm Sensor Tower: about 24.6 million copies and $2.36 billion through launch day. Below is what each number covers, how the estimate grew over 48 hours, how it all compares with GTA 5's record, and what is still unknown.
Update, November 26: this page was first written hours before Take-Two published its figures. The official numbers are now at the top of the table and in the next section; the sections on the Sensor Tower estimate are kept because they explain the platform split and the day-by-day growth, which Take-Two has not published. Our GTA 6 pre-order sales page covers the 32.5 million figure in detail.
How we checked: every figure here appears in at least two independent reports, or is marked with the single outlet that reported it. Estimates are labelled as estimates throughout.
GTA 6 sales at a glance

The official numbers: $3.79 billion and 32.5 million
Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar's parent company, published its first figures in a press release dated November 20, 2026. It says day-one retail sales reached $3.79 billion, based on company estimates through the end of November 19 worldwide, and that the game sold 32.5 million units pre-release, a record across all platforms. It names no platform, edition or digital-versus-physical split, and The Next Web noted that the company did not say how the unit figure was calculated.
Before launch its statements were deliberately vague. On its earnings call on November 9, chief executive Strauss Zelnick said pre-orders were far in excess of the company's expectations and, in the line most outlets quoted, that "we still aren't ready to declare victory."
Why it matters: the two official numbers measure different things. The units are sales before release; the dollars run to the end of launch day. Take-Two has not yet said how many copies have been sold in total.
The Sensor Tower estimate: 24.6 million copies, $2.36 billion
Sensor Tower tracks digital store activity and publishes running estimates. By the evening of launch day, November 19, its tracker showed about 24.58 to 24.59 million copies and roughly $2.36 billion in revenue. Neither Take-Two nor Rockstar has confirmed it.
Three things to know about the figure:

It is cumulative. It includes months of pre-orders, not only copies bought after the midnight unlock.
It covers PlayStation and Xbox. Those are the only platforms the game is on; see GTA 6 platforms.
It does not subtract refunds, as TweakTown points out.

Tip: when you see "GTA 6 sold 24 million in a day", read it as "24 million through its first day, counting pre-orders".
How the estimate grew in 48 hours
The same tracker was quoted at three points, which is why you will find three different numbers online.

When

About 17.1 million

About 24.6 million
About $2.36 billion

The game unlocked at local midnight in each region, starting in New Zealand on November 18; see what time GTA 6 came out. The Wednesday figure is therefore almost entirely pre-orders.
Why it matters: on these estimates, roughly 7.5 million copies and about $700 million were added between Wednesday midday and Thursday night. Most of the launch-day total was already in the bank before anyone played.
PlayStation vs Xbox
Sensor Tower's split is about three to one in PlayStation's favour.

The per-platform figures were reported by GameSpot and repeated by Make Tech Easier. Before launch, Sony said GTA 6 was the most pre-ordered game in the history of the PlayStation Store, and Microsoft said the same for its own store. Neither gave a count.
Why it matters: if you are choosing where to play with friends, far more of them are likely to be on PlayStation. Our best console for GTA 6 comparison covers the other differences.
How it compares with GTA 5's record
GTA 5 set the bar every big launch has been measured against since 2013. Its numbers were official:

GTA 5 (2013)
GTA 6 (2026, estimate)

First day, copies

About 24.6 million

About $2.36 billion

On paper GTA 6 is at more than twice the copies and almost three times the revenue. Two cautions apply. The GTA 5 figure came from the publisher and the GTA 6 figure from an outside firm. And a dollar in 2013 is not a dollar in 2026: the base game costs more now, which is the next point.
Why revenue rose faster than copies
GTA 5 launched at $59.99. GTA 6 costs $79.99 for the Standard Edition and $99.99 for the Ultimate Edition. Dividing Sensor Tower's revenue by its copies gives an average of about $96 per copy. That is our arithmetic on their estimate, not a reported figure, but it suggests either that a large share of early buyers chose the more expensive edition or that the estimate runs high.
Tip: if you have not bought yet, the difference between the two is covered in GTA 6 price and editions and what the Ultimate Edition adds.
What Take-Two and the platform holders have said

Take-Two has described demand with phrases such as "unprecedented" and "far exceeding expectations", without numbers.
Zelnick has said official sales data will be shared soon, and that the company prefers not to claim success before it happens.
Sony and Microsoft each called GTA 6 their store's most pre-ordered game ever, on November 10.

One comparison Zelnick did give is for the previous game: GTA 5 has now sold nearly 235 million copies. That is the long-run number GTA 6 will eventually be measured against.
Has GTA 6 made its budget back?
Rockstar has never published a budget. Reports citing Reuters put the development cost at an estimated $1 billion or more. If the Sensor Tower estimate is close, launch-day revenue alone is more than twice that, before the stores and retailers take their share and before marketing is counted. Our GTA 6 budget page goes through what is and is not known about the cost, and how long GTA 6 was in development explains where the money went.
What analysts expect next
These are forecasts from individual firms, each reported by one outlet we checked:

Take-Two's shares rose about 6% on Wednesday, November 18, and slipped about 1% on launch day itself.
What is not confirmed

Any official unit or revenue figure. Everything above is an estimate or a forecast.
Sales of boxed copies as a separate number. The box contains a download code, so retail copies are redeemed on the same stores; see GTA 6 physical copy.
Regional sales. No report we checked breaks the estimate down by country.
Profit. Revenue is not profit, and Take-Two has not discussed either for launch.

How to read GTA 6 sales headlines

Check the source. "Take-Two announced" is official. "Sensor Tower estimates" or "analysts expect" is not.
Check the window. "First day", "through launch day", "first 24 hours" and "first three days" are different measures.
Check for pre-orders. Almost all early figures include them.
Check the unit. Copies and dollars are often swapped in headlines; 24.6 million is copies, $2.36 billion is revenue.
Ignore numbers with no source at all. Round figures passed around on social media usually trace back to nothing.

What this means for you
For players, the size of the launch matters in two practical ways. A game that sells like this gets long support, so patches and extra content are a safe bet even though Rockstar has dated nothing; see GTA 6 online for what has been said about multiplayer. And critics agree with the buyers: the game sits at 99 on Metacritic, as covered in GTA 6 reviews.
What we will add to this page

Take-Two's first official sales announcement, the moment it is published. One report said it could come as early as Friday, November 20; the company has only said "soon".
First-weekend and first-week figures.
The numbers from Take-Two's next earnings report. The launch falls in its fiscal third quarter, which ends on December 31, 2026.

Q: How much money has GTA 6 made?
A: Take-Two reports $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales worldwide, a company estimate through the end of November 19, 2026. It has not published a total since. Sensor Tower separately estimated about $2.36 billion from digital console sales through launch day.

Q: How many copies of GTA 6 have sold?
A: Take-Two says 32.5 million units were sold before launch and has not given a total since. Sensor Tower estimates about 24.6 million digital console copies through launch day: roughly 18.4 million on PS5 and 6.2 million on Xbox Series X|S.

Q: Did GTA 6 beat GTA 5's first-day sales record?
A: Yes. GTA 5 sold 11.21 million copies worth $815.7 million in its first 24 hours. Take-Two reports $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales for GTA 6 and 32.5 million units sold before launch.

# GTA 6 Adventures in Babysitting Walkthrough: The Vault

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-adventures-in-babysitting-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-25
Status: confirmed

- Adventures in Babysitting is a Jason-only Chapter 4 mission from Andrés de León that opens some time after Making Gainz.
- It starts as errands inside The Vault nightclub and turns into a shootout, a car chase and a helicopter defence.
- Accepting or declining Andrés' drugs changes little: both guides say Jason has to take the drink he is handed afterwards.

This GTA 6 Adventures in Babysitting walkthrough covers Jason's night as nightclub security for Andrés de León, which starts with fetching drinks at The Vault and ends with a rocket launcher in a helicopter. It is one of the longer missions in Chapter 4: PowerPyx counts 20 on-screen objectives. The first half cannot really go wrong. The second half is a run of fights where Jason's health is the thing to watch.
Before you start

Detail

Tip: the mission moves from the club to a chase to a rooftop without a break in either guide's description, so it makes sense to arrive with full health. Enemies drop weapons you can pick up, so ammunition is less of a worry.
Objectives
The 20 objectives PowerPyx lists fall into four stages.

Stage
On-screen objectives

Getting there
Drive to The Vault; Escort Andrés

Inside the club
Order Andrés a drink from the bartender; Give Andrés his drink; Take a picture of Andrés; Talk to the group; Confirm the order with a bartender; Join Andrés' group; Talk to Donatello's security; Take a drink; Return to Andrés' table; Find Andrés in the bathroom; Talk to the dealer; Return to Andrés

Step-by-step
1. Pick up Andrés and drive to The Vault
Go to the house on Starfish Island and follow Paulo around to the back to meet Andrés. He wants a night out, so drive to The Vault nightclub.
2. Get him through the door and fetch a drink
Follow Andrés in. A drunk man stops him at the entrance: step in so Andrés keeps moving. On the first dance floor he asks for a drink. Order it from the bartender on the left. He wants it without lime, but both guides say getting the order wrong does not matter. Bring it to him at the corner by the stairs, take the photo of him and his friends when he hands over his phone, and follow him upstairs.
3. Run the booth upstairs

Talk to the group of girls on the right and invite them to Andrés' booth.
Confirm their order with the bartender nearby.
Sit in the free seat on the couch.
When asked, talk to Donatello's security at the other booth, then go back to Andrés.

4. The drugs and the drink
Andrés offers Jason drugs.

Choice
Result

Accept
No lasting difference (GTABase)

Decline
GTABase says Andrés spikes Jason's drink later anyway

Whatever you pick, the next objective is "Take a drink", and both guides say you cannot refuse it.
5. Find Andrés
Follow Andrés to the DJ booth, the office and back. Push your way out of the DJ booth and look for him at the table. His friends point you to the bathroom on the far side of the floor. He is in the last stall.
6. Collect his delivery
Andrés sends Jason outside for his drugs. Take the main stairs down, leave by the door at the bottom, and walk to the car that pulls up at the end of the alley on the right. Then hurry back to Andrés at the bar in the south-east corner.
7. Protect Andrés in the club
Gunmen from FAP storm the club. PowerPyx describes it as an attempt to kidnap Andrés. Jason's vision is heavily distorted by what he was given, and it stays that way until you are out of the building.

Fight across the floor with Andrés and pick up weapons from fallen enemies.
At the bottom of the stairs, watch for a car full of gunmen, then go through the door on the right.
An attacker tackles Jason: mash the prompt to stop him being stabbed.

Tip: civilians run through the firefight. Both guides advise not hitting them if you want to keep a good Criminal Profile rating.
8. The car escape
Outside, jump into the car with Andrés' security. Jason fires an LMG through the roof: destroy the vehicles chasing you. Both guides warn that he takes heavy damage up there, so keep an eye on his health.
9. Reach the helipad
Leave the car and follow Paulo up the escalator and through the building. At the train tracks, interact with Andrés to help him across, and keep clearing enemies. Take the elevator, follow Paulo onto the roof, clear the helipad and push Andrés into the helicopter.
10. Defend the helicopter

Weapon
How to use it

Assault rifle (unlimited ammo here)
Aim for the enemy helicopters' tail rotors; switch sides of the cabin when prompted

Rocket launcher
Wait for the marker on a helicopter to turn red, then fire

Clearing the helicopters completes the mission. Back at the house, Andrés learns that his son Rafa has been taken.
Where players fail
Neither guide lists formal fail conditions. The objectives are about keeping Andrés safe, and the danger points both guides flag are these.

The LMG section. Jason is exposed through the roof and takes damage quickly, so watch his health bar as well as the cars.
The tackle. Mash the prompt as soon as it appears.
The distorted vision. It does not clear until you leave the club, so check your targets before you fire.
The helicopters. Shooting pilots or gunners is slower than hitting tail rotors.

The club errands, including the wrong drink order, have no penalty.

What comes next
PowerPyx follows this mission with a short separate entry, Rafa's Kidnapping, and then Fresh Evidence; GTABase has no separate page for the kidnapping entry. The two also place the mission differently: PowerPyx puts another short entry, Nate Will Be in Touch, between Dirty Work and this one, while GTABase lists them back to back. Since this mission only needs Making Gainz, it can appear on Jason's map earlier than its place in either list.
For the hardware used at the end, see GTA 6 guns and planes and helicopters. The full story order is in our GTA 6 mission list.

Q: Should you take the drugs in the GTA 6 Adventures in Babysitting walkthrough?
A: It makes no lasting difference, according to GTABase. You can accept or decline, but Jason must take the drink Andrés hands him next, and his vision is distorted for the club fight either way.

Q: How do you start Adventures in Babysitting in GTA 6?
A: Finish Making Gainz and wait for the call to Jason. Then go to Andrés' house on Starfish Island with Jason and follow Paulo around to the back.

Q: How do you shoot down the helicopters at the end?
A: Both guides say to aim the unlimited-ammo assault rifle at the tail rotors, which is quicker than hitting pilots or gunners. With the rocket launcher, wait for the marker on a helicopter to turn red before firing.

Q: Is there a reward for Adventures in Babysitting?
A: PowerPyx lists no reward. GTABase marks the mission as mandatory and required for 100% completion.

# GTA 6 Amateur Hour Walkthrough: Cisco and the Coochie Camper

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-amateur-hour-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-25
Status: confirmed

- Amateur Hour is a Lucia-only Chapter 4 mission given by Francisco "Cisco" Delgado on the Trauma Floor at Ajax Gym.
- Lucia drives Cisco to Washington Island, waits on a bench as bait, then chases the Coochie Camper so Cisco can collect a debt from Judd.
- Shooting out the camper's tyres ends the chase fast, and the mission pays $1,000.

This GTA 6 Amateur Hour walkthrough covers the short Lucia mission where she helps Francisco "Cisco" Delgado get money back from a director who owes him. It is one of the quickest jobs in the build-up to the VCIA Takedown: a drive, a wait on a bench and one chase. The only part that can drag is the chase, and there is a simple way to end it early.
Everything below is described the same way by PowerPyx and GTABase unless we name one of them.
Before you start

Detail

Francisco "Cisco" Delgado

Starts at
The Trauma Floor, Ajax Gym, Vice City

Requirement

Reward

A note on the requirement: PowerPyx calls that first crew workout a separate mission, Blood Sweat and Gear, while GTABase treats it as the last stage of Making Gainz. It is the same workout either way. If Francisco is not on the stage yet, you still have that session to do.
Objectives
PowerPyx lists ten on-screen steps.

Go to the Trauma Floor.
Change outfit at the locker.
Go to Francisco's car.
Go to the pick-up location.
Park the vehicle near the pick-up location.
Wait on the bench.
Stop the Coochie Camper.
Wait for Francisco to get the money.
Drop off Francisco at the back of Ajax Gym.
Park Francisco's car at his spot.

GTABase groups the same mission into five stages.
Step-by-step
1. Talk to Francisco on the Trauma Floor
Go back to Ajax Gym as Lucia and head to the Trauma Floor, the crew's private workout area. Francisco is deadlifting on the stage. Talk to him and he asks for help with a debt.
2. Change at the locker
Use Lucia's locker on the Trauma Floor to change outfit. It is an on-screen objective here, not a cosmetic extra, so do it before you look for Cisco.
3. Follow Cisco to his car
Cisco leaves through the back door of the Trauma Floor. Follow him out to his car. Lucia drives.
4. Drive to the pick-up spot
The pick-up location is a short drive north, on Washington Island. Park in the marked space: parking near the pick-up location is its own objective, and you will be back in the car within a minute.
5. Wait on the bench
Sit on the bench nearby while Cisco hides. Then wait. The Coochie Camper turns up on its own, so there is nothing to do here except stay put.
6. Stop the Coochie Camper
Once the camper arrives, get back into Cisco's car and go after it. Cisco opens fire on it, and you can shoot as well.
Tip: go for the tyres. Both guides say that shooting them is how you stop the camper, and GTABase adds that it comes to a halt almost straight away once they are blown out. Neither guide suggests any other way to stop it. For what Lucia can carry, see GTA 6 weapons.
7. Let Cisco collect
When the camper stops, Judd gets out and Cisco takes his money back. You only have to wait for him to finish.
8. Drive back to Ajax Gym
Take Cisco to the back of Ajax Gym, where you picked him up, and park his car in his own space to finish the mission.
Where players fail
Neither guide lists a fail condition for Amateur Hour, so we will not guess at one. The parts that slow players down are easy to name, though:

Skipping the locker. Changing outfit is an objective, so do it before following Cisco.
Parking loosely. The pick-up spot and Cisco's space at the gym are both marked places, and parking in them is part of the objective list.
Shooting the wrong thing. The tyres are what stop the camper, so aim there from the start.

GTA 6 has no mission replay menu, so if you want a second go, make a manual save first. See how to save in GTA 6 and replaying missions.
Optional goals and rewards

$1,000 (PowerPyx and GTABase)

Nate's text to Lucia, which leads to Cash Injections

100%
GTABase marks the mission as required

What comes next
After Amateur Hour, Nate texts Lucia and asks her to get in touch. PowerPyx lists that call as its own entry, Call Nate, with no reward. GTABase folds it into the start of the next mission. Either way, the next job for Lucia is Cash Injections, a much rougher outing on Ocean Beach.
Just before this mission, the story follows Jason in Too Much Baggage and Watch It. How all of these feed into the airport job is explained in GTA 6 heists, and the full order is in our GTA 6 mission list.

Q: How do you stop the camper in the GTA 6 Amateur Hour walkthrough?
A: Chase the Coochie Camper in Cisco's car and shoot its tyres. Cisco fires too, and Lucia can shoot while driving. GTABase says the camper stops almost at once when the tyres are gone.

Q: How do you start Amateur Hour in GTA 6?
A: Play as Lucia and go back to Ajax Gym after her first workout with Kordell's crew. Francisco is deadlifting on the stage of the Trauma Floor. Talk to him to begin.

Q: What is the reward for Amateur Hour?
A: $1,000, according to both PowerPyx and GTABase. It also leads to Nate's text and the next Lucia mission, Cash Injections.

Q: Can Jason play Amateur Hour?
A: No. PowerPyx marks it as Lucia only, and GTABase lists Lucia as the playable character.

# GTA 6 Cash Injections Walkthrough: Nate's Synthol Deal

This GTA 6 Cash Injections walkthrough covers the mission where Lucia backs Nate up on a Synthol sale that turns into a shootout, a car chase and a motel gunfight. After the easy errand of Amateur Hour, this is a proper combat mission, so stock up on ammo before you call Nate.

Step-by-step
1. Meet Nate and drive to the deal
Meet Nate at the Muscle Beach gym and follow him off the beach to his car. Drive a few blocks north to a back alley and wait for the deal to begin.
2. Open the trunk
When Nate asks, open the trunk and take out the bag. This is where the deal falls apart: the buyers turn on the two of you.

Rushing the motel. Enemies on the upper floor and at the side doors appear after the first group.
Lingering afterwards. Leave straight away. A wanted level has to be lost before you can finish.

# GTA 6 Fresh Evidence Walkthrough: Tiger, Key Card and Mural Door

URL: https://gta6box.com/missions/gta-6-fresh-evidence-walkthrough/
Updated: 2026-11-25
Status: confirmed

- Fresh Evidence is a Jason-only Chapter 4 mission from Dre'Quan that starts at Jack of Hearts and pays $10,000.
- It opens after Watch It and Adventures in Babysitting, and the break-in on Starfish Island happens at night.
- The mural door needs the wall item showing a hand holding a microphone, and the mission ends with a speedboat escape from the police.

This GTA 6 Fresh Evidence walkthrough covers the night Jason and Dre'Quan break into a mansion on Starfish Island to copy blackmail material. It is a stealth mission for the first two thirds, with a guard to hide, a tiger to work around and a small wall puzzle, and a shootout and boat chase for the last third.

Tip: the mission ends in a gunfight you cannot avoid, so arrive with body armour and ammo even though it starts quietly. A manual save first does no harm either: see how to save in GTA 6.

Step-by-step
1. Meet Dre'Quan at Jack of Hearts
Go to Dre'Quan's office as Jason, tell him you are ready and follow him to the car in the alley. Drive to Starfish Island. The break-in happens at night, so the game has you wait until dark.
2. Get inside
Dre'Quan stops at a wall. Climb it, then climb the boxes to the upper floor and go into the workout room. There is one guard on the far side of it.

Knock the guard out.
Carry the body to the closet Dre'Quan opens and leave it there.
Follow the walkway to the door at its end and open it with the Snap Gun.

3. Take the key card from the bedroom
Follow the hallways to the bedroom. A tiger lives in this house. On this stretch it wanders out onto the balcony, so keep away from it and keep moving. The key card is on the side table to the left of the bed.
4. Leave by the balcony and distract the guards
When you turn back, the tiger is in the hallway. Do not try to pass it. Follow Dre'Quan out onto the balcony and drop down onto the cabanas by the pool.
Two guards stand between you and the elevator. Follow the wall on the right side of the pool to the bar, pick up a bottle and throw it to the left of the guards. They go to look, and the way is clear.
5. Lure the tiger with raw meat
The tiger has moved again, this time into the living room you need to cross. Open the fridge on the right, take the raw meat and throw it to the far side of the room. Once the tiger goes after it, follow Dre'Quan to the elevator and ride down to the basement.
6. Open the hidden door
Downstairs, go to the round room with the large gold mural. Dre'Quan settles who has to open the door with a game of rock paper scissors. Both guides say Jason only has to solve the puzzle if he loses.

If Jason loses
What to do

Find the item
Match the symbols on the mural to the empty slot in the wall

The right one
The item with a hand holding a microphone, on the blue part of the wall at the far right

Use it
Pull it off the wall, place it in the slot, then hold the prompt to open the door

7. Copy the evidence
Squeeze through after Dre'Quan into the surveillance room. He starts copying the files. Interact with him to watch the videos while the copy runs.
8. Fight back to the elevator
The quiet part is over. There are guns on the wall of the surveillance room: take one or two before you leave. Guards come into the basement as you step out. Clear them and take the elevator back up.
9. Cross the upper floor and reach the dock
Fight across the upper floor to the far balcony. Enemies wait around the corners here, so check each one before you run through. Jump down at the same spot you used earlier and head for the dock. PowerPyx notes that you are still under fire on the way.
10. Escape by speedboat
Get into Dante's speedboat and drive away. The police join in at this point. Keep going until you lose them and the mission completes. If the stars are slow to drop, how the GTA 6 wanted level works explains what breaks the search, and GTA 6 boats covers boat handling.
Where players fail

The hallway after the key card. The tiger blocks it. The balcony is the intended way out.
The two elevator guards. The bottle goes to their left, away from the route you want to take.
The living room. Throw the meat to the far side so the tiger ends up away from your path.
The escape. Guards arrive in the basement and on the upper floor. Take the wall guns and do not sprint around blind corners.
